\section{Claim register}\label{sec:claims}
\subsection{Right-ideal semantics}\hypertarget{claim:semantics}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN.} Literal ordered membership and relation-respecting quotient right-action operation in the original ring. RightIdealBridge connects the displayed two-generator semiring carrier to a RingRightIdeal under explicit negation closure and proves quotient action laws; SupportDimension proves zero-quotient/membership equivalence and consumes explicit bottom-dimension/support/zero equivalences. OriginalCentralSupport gives the actual original-ring quotient and central-support zero bridge. CharacteristicSupport constructs a finite associated-layer support proxy from actual quotient classes, while SpecCharacteristicSupport identifies the genuine Module.support over a supplied commutative associated module and states its annihilator zero-locus boundary. ActualClassSupport connects a genuine filtered-layer quotient to that support boundary and records the WithBot/integer-defect correspondence under explicit class-map data. M01StructuralBoundary and the sequence-ring label obstruction show that the historical proposition-only class scaffold does not imply structural filtered-algebra facts; M01AssociatedGradedBoundary shows generic filtration data need not have commutative associated layers, CentralFieldFiltrationBoundary exposes an incompatible degree-zero field-image requirement, M01DegreeZeroBridge proves the scalar/degree-zero additive equivalence once the stronger central-field interface is supplied, and M01StructuralClass supplies an additive filtered-ring interface with consecutive layers and least-layer detection. AssociatedGradedSpecBridge consumes an explicit quotient-layer map to a commutative associated module and proves support/annihilator zero-locus consequences; M01AssociatedSpecAdapter attaches such explicit commutative data to the structural M01 class. CharacteristicSupportProducer consumes explicit per-prime ambient producers and localized common-quotient zero bridges to prove a genuine module-support inclusion. The full filtered-class/Spec(gr U) construction remains open. TerminalBoundary extracts literal original-U cofactors from a supplied zero quotient or membership witness, while Package/Opposite transports left S1 to right S1 in the opposite ring and conversely.

\subsection{Scalar-pencil utility}\hypertarget{claim:scalar}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN.} Finite exceptional scalars and simultaneous forbidden-set avoidance for finite division-ring coordinates and central-field matrix blocks with nonzero starting coordinates. PencilBridge, ActivatedPencil, MatrixPencil, DivisionLLD and RadicalLift conditionally infer top-to-cyclic, finite affine-source or finite top-lifting consequences from supplied data. FiniteOrbitPencil derives finite exceptions from an actual finite orbit basis over a commutative scalar extension while preserving the ordered activated identity; DerivedOrbitPencil constructs that orbit basis under an explicit finite central-dimension hypothesis. JacobsonScalarExtension packages the same top comparison through the actual Jacobson quotient while retaining the scalar-extension orbit basis, ExplicitBlocks consumes explicit finite composition, division-ring or repeated matrix block data, IsotypicBlocks exposes the remaining noncommutative repeated-block finite-bad-set theorem, and DivisionEigenBoundary isolates that witness family as an explicit hypothesis. DivisionEigenObstruction supplies a zero-pencil counterexample showing finite generation alone cannot imply finite bad sets. FiniteCentralDivisionPencil supplies the finite-dimensional-over-the-center division-block bridge, FiniteCentralDivisionLLD gives a determinant-free finite-spectrum variant under an explicit split map, and FiniteCentralDivisionActivated composes it with the actual Jacobson-top/right-cyclic consumer while preserving the ordered pencil identity. WeightedDetectionComposition composes finite triangular detection with a nilpotent right correction. The scalar-extension theorem still requires the finite orbit basis and top comparison, and does not handle arbitrary noncommutative endomorphism division rings. Repeated simple factors beyond these explicit block consumers, radical construction and the arbitrary finite-length activation theorem remain open M06–M07 work.

\subsection{Divisor-indexed assembly}\hypertarget{claim:assembly-scaffold}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN-SCAFFOLD.} Given DivisorIndexedAssembly with a source and literal original cofactors for every nonzero divisor, extract SameDivisorS1. Sources may depend on d. OriginalTestContract records the M06 original-U finite-test/source witness shape; DivisionLLD and DivisionLLDList add concrete finite affine source-avoidance families with arbitrary offsets and nonzero tails, with the list-indexed interface preserving one multiplier for every test and removing source-zero scalars; OriginalDivisionProducer constructs one literal nonzero original-U affine source from a certified finite list carrying explicit division-coefficient pencil bridges, and its ActualOriginalDivisionTest bridge derives that source from genuine finite division-ring top data and cyclicity equivalences. The finite-direction constructor `exists\_original\_affine\_source\_of\_actual\_directions` makes the required original-U directions and bridge data explicit and retains all tests. FiniteDimensionalProducer selects one common original-U source from split finite-dimensional pencils while retaining ordered passes; FiniteDimensionalAssembly packages those selectors into per-divisor SameDivisorS1 data; FiniteTestFamilyAssembly retains every offset, nonzero right tail and admissibility field through that assembly; LocalizedDivisorAssembly instead consumes actual right-localized identities and denominator inverses to produce the same assembly; FullSymbolFiniteAssembly clears a finite family with one supplied common right denominator before original cofactor extraction; WeylA1Calibration supplies a literal original-ring A1 identity and a Stafford38 finite-potential adapter as a concrete calibration. WeylHigherDimensionalMonicization extends this calibration to every positive-rank presented Weyl tower, giving scalar-or-outer-monic alternatives and an exact original-ring remainder factorization, but no support-vanishing claim. WeylHigherDimensionalArbitraryMonic extends the division certificate to arbitrary coefficient-left outer monics with an explicit finite remainder bound, still without support vanishing. FiniteLengthSourceMapBoundary independently shows that finite length and a top bridge alone do not produce an original-U source map. OriginalOrbitProducer weakens source selection to explicit finite orbit bases for each cyclic image and retains all finite tests. OriginalFiniteCoefficientSource records a concrete finite coefficient subring, membership, retained tests and original cofactors while leaving coefficient data as explicit inputs. WeylHigherDimensionalEvolutionary supplies bounded finite-potential certificates in the original higher-rank Weyl tower, and the degree-one monic endpoint combines its remainder with a literal AssemblyWitness. OriginalTestProducerBoundary gives an independent admissibility counterexample showing that the current abstract contract does not itself produce an affine source; Assembly still routes only a supplied composite producer to this consumer. DifferentialOreDescent adds a finite-cover clearance consumer under explicit commutative-coefficient, filtration-lowering, power-Ore and whole-chart central-S1 hypotheses. This supplies no general instance or producer; finite CandidateFamily and uniform SingleSourceAssembly are optional toy contracts.

\subsection{Finite-length boundary}\hypertarget{claim:length-scaffold}{}\backmap
\textbf{LEAN-SCAFFOLD.} MinimalPrimeLength wraps composition-series and finite-length closure facts and, given a supplied local model with Noetherian and Artinian hypotheses at a minimal support point, derives finite length and finite generation. MinimalPrimeLocalTheorem supplies a commutative local Noetherian theorem deriving finite length from a finite module whose maximal ideal is minimal over its actual annihilator. FilteredMinimalPrimeBridge derives the minimal-annihilator condition and finite length over an actual `Localization.AtPrime p` from support dimension zero. RightFiltration supplies an explicit finite right-module composition filtration with maximal adjacent inclusions and quotient data; ActualRadicalTop extracts finite generation, finite length, and Jacobson-quotient cyclicity from such a genuine filtration; GoodLocalBridge derives local finite generation, Noetherianity and finite length from explicit surjective and Artinian inputs. JacobsonTop proves actual radical-quotient generation reflection for finitely generated right modules, ActivatedFiniteLength consumes that criterion for an arbitrary finite family of supplied top blocks while retaining the ordered pencil identity, JacobsonScalarExtension packages the same top comparison through an actual Jacobson quotient and a supplied commutative scalar-extension orbit basis, ExplicitBlocks consumes explicit finite composition/division-ring/matrix block data, FiniteCentralDivisionPencil supplies finite bad-set bounds when division blocks are finite-dimensional over the central field, FiniteCentralDivisionActivated composes those bounds with the Jacobson-top activated consumer, and MinimalPrimeCentralActivated composes the local minimal-prime finite-length certificate with that activation. GradedFilteredLength adds exact one-step length additivity after an explicit R-linear quotient equivalence to the localized graded factor; GradedLengthFilteredChainBoundary gives a strict filtered inclusion with surjective induced layers, so a separate strictness/Zariskian theorem is required for iteration. BoundedBelowStrictnessContract gives a sufficient exhaustive monotone Nat-indexed bounded-below criterion for strict-layer visibility, and StrictFiniteGradedChain proves the finite-filtration version with an explicit non-surjective associated layer. These modules construct no characteristic support, localization or full minimal-prime bridge for the noncommutative paper module.
